svg.title: MCP distillation detail
svg.desc: A component-level view of the local two-agent distillation, all of it on the developer's machine. The orchestrating coding agent spawns two role-locked subagents and holds the three setup tools that belong to neither role: get_role_definitions, import_session and manage_consent. REVIEW_ASSIST_ROLE decides which tools the server registers, so the other role's tools are absent rather than merely disallowed. The Author holds this session's transcript and is registered eight tools: get_generation_guide, list_transcripts, get_spine, read_transcript, compute_diff, read_diff, get_questions and answer_questions. The Intent Reviewer reads the diff cold with no transcript tools and no file-reading tools, and is registered eight of its own: get_generation_guide, compute_diff, read_diff, get_reviewer_instructions, record_interview_round, get_answers, submit_document and set_consent. compute_diff opens the run and returns the run_id, the numbered hunk index, the SHAs, the consent state and whether a .reviewer folder exists; it returns no diff text, which read_diff pages. The two role sessions are separate processes, and the run file at ~/.review-assist/runs/<run_id>.json is the only thing they share: the reviewer records questions and gets a q_id for each, the author answers by q_id, and the reviewer reads those answers back in the author's own words. The repository's .reviewer folder carries its own house rules, served to the reviewer by get_reviewer_instructions after the diff and before round one; it adds questions but cannot relax a check. submit_document is the reviewer's call alone and gates the write behind repository consent, head drift, anchor resolution, interview attestation and the validator's five checks, then writes .intent/<branch>.json. The run leaves two outputs: the Intent Document for the human who will review the pull request, and the reviewer's closing message for the session that can still fix the code.
svg.text: Review Assist: component-level view of the local two-agent distillation
one server process per role · stdio · no model calls
Spawns both role-locked subagents, relays the q_ids, and drives the run.
It never reads the run, so the reviewer's closing message is its only report.
Both roles are subagents of this agent. Neither is a process it talks to over a network.
REVIEW_ASSIST_ROLE decides which tools are registered.
The other role's tools are absent, not merely refused.
Claude Code's tools: allowlist is belt and braces.
JSONL on disk, read end to end through get_spine.
It never leaves the machine, and no reviewer tool reaches it.
No submit_document. No set_consent. It answers; it does not judge.
No transcript tools, and no file-reading tools at all.
Everything it knows about intent, it had to ask for.
No list_transcripts. No get_spine. No read_transcript.
Returns the run_id, the numbered hunk index (H1...Hn), the base and
head SHAs, this repo's consent state, and whether .reviewer/ exists.
It returns no diff text: read_diff pages the change, hunk by hunk.
Outside the repository. The two role sessions are separate
processes, and this file is the only thing they share.
The interview: two-sided, and attested by the server
answered_by: author is attested; a transcribed answer is not.
submit stamps meta.interview from the run, never from a self-report.
What only the Author can supply
· the ask, in the user's own words
· what was tried and abandoned, and why it lost
· what was run, and what was not
A recorded non-answer is worth more than an invented one: the
author answers with resolved: false and says what is missing.
None of this is recoverable from the diff, which is why the
reviewer has to ask rather than read.
1 Repository consent: always, once or never
2 Head drift: a branch that moved is a different change
3 Anchors must resolve to hunk ids from this run
On pass it writes .intent/<branch>.json and returns the PR block.
The run stays open: a fix is an edit and a resubmit, never a re-ask.
Markdown at the repo root, committed with the code and reviewed
like anything else. Most repositories need none.
· Served by get_reviewer_instructions: the reviewer reads no files.
· Read after the diff, before round one, so it lands in round one.
· It adds questions. It cannot relax a check or excuse a round.
· Untrusted repo data: reference material, never a second protocol.
The document reaches the human who will review the pull request.
The closing message reaches the session that can still fix the code.
committed with the code; the GitHub App validates and renders it
Open questions, everything in verification.not_verified, and any
defect the cold read exposed. It goes back to the coding agent.
The server never calls a model. It computes the ground truth (the diff), serves the source (the transcript, the house rules), and gates the result (the validator).
The findings leave the run twice, because the human reviewing the pull request arrives after the fact and the session that can still fix the code never sees the run.
